title: OET Scores: 0–500, A–E and the Grade You Need
summary: How OET's per-sub-test score and grade work, why Grade B is the common target, and how to reach the bar in every skill.

nodes.label: Per sub-test
nodes.note: A score and grade for each of the 4 skills

chunks.heading: A score and grade per sub-test
chunks.body: OET reports a **numerical score from 0 to 500 (in 10-point steps)** for **each of the four sub-tests**, mapped to a **letter grade A to E**. There's **no single overall score** — your **Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking are each graded separately**.
chunks.realExample: You might get Listening 380 (B), Reading 420 (B), Writing 360 (B), Speaking 340 (C) — each skill has its own number and grade, and regulators read them individually.
chunks.memoryHook: 0–500 + A–E for EACH skill. No overall — every sub-test stands alone.

chunks.heading: Grade B is the usual target
chunks.body: Many healthcare regulators and visa routes require **Grade B (a score of about 350) in every sub-test**. Because each skill is judged separately, **your weakest sub-test is the constraint** — a strong Reading can't rescue a Speaking below B.
chunks.realExample: If your council needs B in all four but your Writing is a C, you don't meet the requirement despite three Bs — the weakest sub-test decides whether you qualify.
chunks.memoryHook: Usually you need Grade B (~350) in ALL four. The weakest sub-test decides it.

chunks.heading: Fix the weakest sub-test
chunks.body: Since every skill must clear the bar, **identify your lowest sub-test and focus practice there**. For most candidates that's **Writing or Speaking** (the profession-specific, human-judged ones), so targeted work on task selection and communication pays off most.
chunks.realExample: If Writing is your weak point, drill selecting relevant information and organising the referral letter — lifting that one sub-test to B can be what finally meets the requirement.
chunks.memoryHook: Every skill must pass — so pour practice into your weakest sub-test.

chunks.heading: Check the exact requirement and retake if needed
chunks.body: Requirements **differ by regulator, country and visa route**, so **confirm the exact grade** you need before booking. If one sub-test falls short, you can **retake** — and in some cases combine sub-test results across sittings (check your authority's rules).
chunks.realExample: Two authorities may both accept OET but require different grades — verify yours, and if only one skill is short, a focused retake is faster than resitting everything.
chunks.memoryHook: Confirm the exact grade you need; retake the weak skill rather than the whole test.

recall.a: A numerical score from 0 to 500 (in 10-point steps) and a letter grade A–E for each of the four sub-tests — there's no single overall score.

recall.q: What grade do healthcare regulators commonly require?
recall.a: Grade B (about 350) in every sub-test, though it varies by authority.

recall.q: Why does your weakest sub-test matter most?
recall.a: Each skill is graded separately and must clear the bar, so a strong skill can't compensate for a weak one.

recall.q: Which sub-tests are most often the weak point?
recall.a: Writing and Speaking — the profession-specific, human-judged ones — so they usually deserve the most focused practice.

recall.q: What should you do before booking, and if one skill falls short?
recall.a: Confirm the exact grade your regulator/visa route requires, and if one sub-test is short, consider a focused retake.
